name: Role changed in a workspace
description: Sent when someone's permissions in a shared workspace are changed, showing the old and new role side by side and spelling out what the person can and can no longer do.

origin.note: Design: permissions diff — the workspace as eyebrow, the old and new role as a two-up comparison, and the consequences as paired inventories of what is now allowed and what is not.

subject: You're now {{ new_role }} in {{ workspace_name }}
preheader: What the new role lets you do, and what it no longer does.

workspace_name.description: Which workspace this concerns, used as the eyebrow. Someone who belongs to eleven of them needs this before anything else on the page.

heading_lead.description: The words before the role in the headline. Kept separate so the role itself can be any noun without the sentence needing an article that agrees with it.

new_role.description: The role now in force, exactly as it is named in the product. Inventing a friendlier word here means the reader cannot find it in the interface.

previous_role.description: The role held until now. Present so the reader can tell whether this was a promotion or a restriction without having to remember what they had.

previous_label.description: Caption printed under the old role. It sits a step smaller and muted beneath the role itself, so keep it to one word — the two columns stack at 320px.

new_label.description: Caption printed under the new role.

body.description: One sentence on what changed and where. Do not congratulate: a role change is as often a restriction as a promotion, and the same email is sent either way.
body.default: Your permissions in this workspace have been updated. Everything already shared with you is still there — only what you are allowed to do with it has changed.

gained_label.description: Small heading over the list of new abilities.

gained.description: Abilities the new role adds, as `text` and optional `detail` pairs. Write them as actions the person would take, not as permission constants from your authorisation layer.

example.detail: Including ones created by other members

lost_label.description: Small heading over the list of removed abilities.
lost_label.default: What you can no longer do

lost.description: Abilities the new role removes, in the same shape. This is the list people actually need and the one most products leave out — an empty array simply hides the section.

changed_by.description: Who made the change. Attribution turns an anonymous permission drop into something the reader can take up with a colleague instead of with support.

changed_by_prefix.description: The words before the name in the attribution bar, separated so a translation can reorder them.

changed_at.description: When the change took effect. Optional: some directories sync roles in bulk and cannot say honestly when a given one moved.

changed_at_prefix.description: The words before the timestamp in the attribution bar.

button_label.description: Label on the link into the workspace. Send them to the thing itself, not to a settings page about it.

workspace_url.description: Where the workspace lives, so the reader can confirm what they see against what this email claims.

closing_note.description: The route to a correction. Roles are set by people, and people make mistakes, so say who can undo this rather than making the reader guess.
closing_note.default: Roles are set by the owners of a workspace, not by us. If this does not look right, ask an owner to change it back.
